---
# Developer CLI tools role
# Tools: bat, bats, gh, glab, diffnav, gh-dash, gh-notify, eza, git-delta, git-graph, tldr, glow, gum, vhs, freeze, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, superfile, tmux, sesh, worktrunk, workmux, zellij, herdr, btop, htop, duckdb, rclone, coreutils, taplo, television, pandoc, tailspin, lnav, grc, ccze (Linux only), dasel, yq, jnv, witr, figlet, toilet, lolcat, fastfetch

# =============================================================================
# macOS - all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Tap diffnav formula (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: dlvhdr/formulae
    state: present

- name: Tap raine/workmux formula (macOS)
  # workmux is a tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with first-class agent
  # status icons (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done) rendered into the tmux
  # window list. Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md
  # for the wt-vs-wm split.
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: raine/workmux
    state: present

# Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate: `brew install` refuses to
# load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted
# ("Error: Refusing to load formula <tap>/<formula> from untrusted tap"). The
# homebrew_tap module has no trust parameter, so trust via `brew trust`.
# Idempotent + back-compatible: older Homebrew has no trust concept, so
# `tap-info` won't contain "Untrusted" and the trust task no-ops (no version
# gate needed). Keep this loop in sync with the third-party taps above — add any
# new third-party tap here too. See pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
  loop:
    - dlvhdr/formulae
    - raine/workmux
  register: devtools_tap_info
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.item }}"
  changed_when: true

- name: Install developer CLI tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - bat
      - bats-core
      - gh
      - glab
      - diffnav
      - git-delta
      - git-graph
      - eza
      - tlrc
      - glow
      - gum
      - vhs
      - freeze
      - thefuck
      - zoxide
      - direnv
      - yazi
      - superfile
      - tmux
      - sesh
      - worktrunk
      - workmux
      - zellij
      # herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator. Trial tool
      # that COEXISTS with tmux/zellij (you run one or the other); not a
      # replacement. Config in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
      - herdr
      - btop
      - htop
      - duckdb
      - rclone
      - coreutils
      - taplo
      - television
      - pandoc
      - tailspin
      - lnav
      - grc
      - dasel
      - yq
      - jnv
      - witr
      - figlet
      - toilet
      - lolcat
      - fastfetch
      # Shell linting / formatting. Bundled binaries are also pulled by the
      # `shellcheck-py` and `pre-commit-shfmt` repos in .pre-commit-config.yaml,
      # but having them on PATH lets `just lint-shell` skip the uvx wrapper
      # and gives users `shellcheck file.sh` / `shfmt -d file.sh` for ad-hoc
      # checking. ~1 MB each, no transitive deps.
      - shellcheck
      - shfmt
      # actionlint - static checker for GitHub Actions workflows. Type-checks
      # ${{ }} expressions, validates uses:/runner/cron, and pipes each run:
      # block through shellcheck (installed above) + Python through pyflakes.
      # Also driven by the rhysd/actionlint pre-commit hook (actionlint-system,
      # which reuses this on-PATH binary). See docs/tools/actionlint.md.
      - actionlint
    state: present
    # Note: ccze is not available on Homebrew (removed from homebrew-core).
    # It is installed only on Linux via apt; the `lessl` zsh wrapper is guarded
    # on `command -v ccze` so it becomes a no-op on macOS.

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)
# =============================================================================

# --- gh ---
- name: Check if gh is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: gh --version
  register: gh_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Set gh release architecture
  # Broadened to RedHat + decoupled from gh_check (sudo-path) so the
  # user-level fallback below works on CentOS 7 where the .deb install is
  # skipped entirely. set_fact is cheap; safe to always compute.
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    gh_release_arch: >-
      {{
        'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
        else ''
      }}

- name: Skip gh on unsupported architecture
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gh_check.rc != 0
    - gh_release_arch == ''
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "gh skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"

- name: Install gh from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gh_check.rc != 0
    - gh_release_arch != ''
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Get latest gh release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: gh_release

    - name: Download gh .deb package
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/{{ gh_release.json.tag_name }}/gh_{{ gh_release.json.tag_name | regex_replace('^v', '') }}_linux_{{ gh_release_arch }}.deb"
        dest: /tmp/gh.deb
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Install gh .deb package
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: /tmp/gh.deb

    - name: Clean up gh .deb
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/gh.deb
        state: absent

  rescue:
    - name: Warn gh installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "gh installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"

    - name: Clean up gh temp files after failure
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/gh.deb
```

# NOTE: thefuck is now installed via uv tool (python_uv_tools role)
# This avoids conda/virtualenv Python path conflicts

# --- shellcheck + shfmt ---
# Shell linting / formatting. macOS gets both via brew (block above).
# Linux: shellcheck is in standard Debian/Ubuntu apt; shfmt is a Go binary
# not in apt main — best-effort install via Linuxbrew if present, else the
# user can `go install mvdan.cc/sh/v3/cmd/shfmt@latest` or rely on the
# pre-commit-shfmt hook which bundles its own binary.
# actionlint (GitHub Actions linter) rides the same Linuxbrew best-effort
# path — not in apt; on non-Linuxbrew Linux hosts the rhysd/actionlint
# pre-commit hook still lints workflows (bundles its own binary via Go).
- name: Install shellcheck (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: shellcheck
    state: present

- name: Detect Linuxbrew for shfmt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: shfmt_brew_probe
  changed_when: false

- name: Install shfmt via Linuxbrew when available (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - shfmt_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: shfmt
    state: present

- name: Install actionlint via Linuxbrew when available (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - shfmt_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: actionlint
    state: present

# --- direnv ---
- name: Install direnv (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: direnv
    state: present

- name: Check installed direnv version
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    if [ -x "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/direnv" ]; then
      "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/direnv" --version | sed 's/^v//'
    elif command -v direnv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      direnv --version | sed 's/^v//'
    else
      echo "0.0.0"
    fi
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: direnv_version
  changed_when: false

- name: Set direnv release architecture
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - direnv_version.stdout | trim is version('2.32.1', '<')
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    direnv_release_arch: >-
      {{
        'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
        else 'arm' if target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armv6l', 'arm']
        else target_architecture
      }}
```

# Plan: Install `mosh` across all profiles via the `devtools` role

## Context

The user wants [mosh](https://mosh.org/) (mobile shell — a roaming, UDP-based SSH replacement that survives network changes and latency) installed on **all profiles**. The `devtools` role is the right home: it runs **unconditionally** on macOS + both Ubuntu profiles (`dot_ansible/playbooks/{macos,linux}.yml` include `- role: devtools` with no `when:` gate), so anything added there lands on every managed host — exactly "all profiles."

mosh is a trivial package to install: `brew install mosh` on macOS and `apt install mosh` on Debian/Ubuntu (universe/main). It is not currently installed or referenced anywhere in `dot_ansible/` (only mentioned in prose in `docs/tools/clipboard*.md` re: OSC 52). This mirrors the existing `shellcheck` install exactly (brew on mac, one-liner apt task on Linux).

## Scope decision

- **Targets**: macOS + `ubuntu_desktop` + `ubuntu_server` (the repo's three profiles). RedHat/CentOS is **out of scope** — there is no first-class RedHat profile, and most of `devtools` only special-cases Debian + Darwin. (mosh is in EPEL if ever needed; not adding it.)
- **Firewall/runtime heads-up (not implemented)**: `mosh-server` listens on UDP `60000–61000`. On cloud `ubuntu_server` hosts behind a security group / ufw, the user must open that UDP range for inbound mosh sessions. This is deployment config, not install, so it stays out of this change — noted here only so it isn't a surprise.

## Changes

### 1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`

- **macOS**: add `- mosh` to the `name:` list in the **"Install developer CLI tools (macOS)"** `community.general.homebrew` task (the same list that holds `htop`, `rclone`, `shellcheck`, etc.).
- **Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)**: add a new apt task following the existing `shellcheck` one-liner pattern (around `main.yml:2092`):
  \```yaml
  # --- mosh ---
  # mosh (mobile shell) — roaming UDP-based SSH replacement; survives IP
  # changes / sleep / high latency. In Debian/Ubuntu apt (universe). Note:
  # mosh-server listens on UDP 60000-61000, which cloud hosts must open.
  - name: Install mosh (Debian/Ubuntu)
    when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    become: true
    tags: [sudo]
    ansible.builtin.apt:
      name: mosh
      state: present
  \```
- **Header comment**: append `mosh` to the `# Tools: ...` list at the top of the file (`main.yml:5`).

### 2. `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` (CLAUDE.md cross-file rule: new tool → A–Z row)

- Add A–Z index row in alphabetical position (after the `l*` rows, before `n*`): `| **mosh** | brew | apt | devtools |`.
- Add `mosh` to the `devtools/tasks/main.yml:` enumeration bullet (~line 194) and, for completeness, the brew-side + apt-side per-manager catalog lists (the same lists that name `shellcheck`/`htop`).

### 3. `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.zh-TW.md` (bilingual mirror)

- Mirror the same A–Z row `| **mosh** | brew | apt | devtools |` (near line 985, after the `htop` row region / alphabetical `m` slot) and add `mosh` to the devtools enumeration bullet (~line 187).

### Not changed (verified)

- **README.md** — its "What You Get" lists *config files*, not the devtools CLI tool set, so no per-tool row exists to update. No change.
- **No chezmoi prompt / no new install mechanism** — `just gen-prompts`, completions, and the tool-managers Decision-tree / Per-manager *mechanism* subsections don't apply (mosh is a new tool through existing brew+apt mechanisms).

## Verification

1. **Ansible syntax** — `just` / `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` on the devtools play, e.g.
   `cd dot_ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --syntax-check --tags devtools` (and `macos.yml`).
2. **Docs build** — `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (added table rows only; nav unchanged). Expect only the known baseline warnings tracked in `backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`.
3. **End-to-end (the real check)** — apply the devtools role on this host and confirm the binary:
   - macOS: `chezmoi apply` (or targeted ansible run) → `mosh --version` / `command -v mosh` and `command -v mosh-server`.
   - Linux: same, expecting the apt package.
   Optionally smoke a loopback session: `mosh localhost -- true` (needs UTF-8 locale + sshd; may not be available on all hosts — report if skipped).

```
